The coordinator already serializes release allocation and authenticates the historical v0.6.13 tuple, so it should remain alive while the tag-bound verifier completes, then authorize the existing publisher.
decisions: Set Automatic Release coordinate timeout-minutes to 35 and use a 30-minute explicit wall-clock verifier deadline.

Dispatch release.yaml at the immutable tag with return_run_details=true; consume only its direct positive workflow_run_id, with no workflow-run list fallback or assumption that the response contains run_attempt.

Immediately GET and validate that exact run ID to capture its positive initial run_attempt, then poll only the same ID/attempt; after success resolve current protected refs/heads/main, create or reuse the deterministic handoff, and dispatch publish-release.yaml at main with the existing full tuple.
Preserve release.yaml verification/evidence stages and keep publish-release.yaml unchanged.
Treat v0.6.13 recovery as the only release outcome of the corrective merge; no v0.6.14 may be allocated while it is pending.

perspectives.assessment: The verifier currently has an unnecessary write boundary. Authorization must come only from trusted current-main coordinator code and must be bound to immutable identities on every observation, not inferred from timestamps or workflow listings.
required_controls: Remove release.yaml dispatch-publish and any verifier actions: write or checks: write scope.
Reject an absent, malformed, zero, negative, non-integer, or ambiguous direct dispatch workflow_run_id; do not require run_attempt in that response and never list runs as fallback.

Immediately GET the exact returned workflow_run_id; validate its ID, positive run_attempt, name, path, event, repository, tag/head branch, and source SHA before capturing that run_attempt, then revalidate the same complete identity on every poll.
Fail immediately on attempt rollover, API error, identity drift, unsupported status, failure, cancelled, timed_out, or 30-minute deadline expiry.
Resolve the publisher revision only after exact verifier success and bind it into the deterministic handoff external_id.
Bind the handoff details_url to the exact verifier run/attempt and reject duplicate or non-exact candidate checks.
Permit release/package mutation only through unchanged publish-release.yaml after it revalidates the full tuple.
residual_risks: GitHub dispatch response semantics are platform-critical; a missing or changed return_run_details workflow_run_id contract, or a failing/mismatched immediate exact-ID GET, must stop recovery rather than trigger correlation heuristics.
A coordinator runner interruption after verifier success but before publisher dispatch requires a serialized exact-tuple retry; duplicate/forged checks must remain fail-closed.
Live publication is irreversible at the package/release layer, so all fake-API and required CI gates must pass before merge.

perspectives.assessment: Tests must execute the coordinator state machine with injectable time and fake GitHub endpoints. Text-only workflow assertions are necessary for permissions and unchanged publisher policy but are insufficient for dispatch/poll/handoff behavior.

no publisher dispatch before exact handoff

consensus.summary: Implement a minimal high-risk trust-boundary correction in which Automatic Release accepts the directly returned verifier workflow_run_id, immediately GETs and validates that exact run to capture its initial attempt, polls only the same ID/attempt, then creates the existing deterministic handoff and dispatches the unchanged publisher. Remove all verifier-side dispatch/write authority. Fail closed on every ambiguity. Let the merged correction's exact-main CI recover v0.6.13 automatically and validate published evidence before cleanup.
non_negotiable_sequence: Authenticate exact-main CI and recover the existing v0.6.13 tuple.
Dispatch tag-bound Release Verify with return_run_details=true and validate its direct positive workflow_run_id without assuming the response contains run_attempt.
Immediately GET and validate that exact ID, capture its positive initial run_attempt, and poll only that same ID/attempt to exact success within 30 minutes under a 35-minute coordinator timeout.
Create or exactly reuse one tuple/details-url-bound successful handoff check.
Dispatch unchanged Publish Release at main with the existing full tuple.
Validate artifacts and close/clean tracking state only after live success.
assumptions: GitHub's dispatch endpoint used by actions/github-script supports return_run_details=true and directly returns a positive workflow_run_id plus URLs, but not run_attempt; implementation must immediately GET that exact ID to validate identity and capture a positive initial run_attempt, and must fail if either contract is unavailable.
Issue #93 remains the durable tracking issue for this correction.
Protected main and tag rules remain active; implementation must query explicit refs and must not trust local CLI defaults.
